Standard exercism paasio. What the consistency test requires is that ReadCount returns a consistent snapshot: `nops == n/numBytes`. Since each read is exactly numBytes (nopReader returns len(p)), nops must equal the number of completed reads, and n must equal the number of completed bytes — both must be captured atomically. Use a mutex to update both counters, and use a mutex for ReadCount as well.

Note: the test checks `int64(nops) != expectedOps`, where expectedOps = n/numBytes. If the counters are updated atomically (bytes and ops together), then at any snapshot nops == n/numBytes holds exactly. Good.

All tests pass with the race detector enabled. Done. Let me summarize briefly.

All tests pass, including under the race detector.

## What I implemented in `paasio.go`

The interfaces (`ReadCounter`, `WriteCounter`, `ReadWriteCounter`) were already declared in `interface.go`, so I only added the concrete types and constructors:

- **`readCounter`** — wraps an `io.Reader`; `Read` delegates to the underlying reader, then records the returned byte count and one operation under a mutex. `ReadCount` returns both counters as a single atomic snapshot.
- **`writeCounter`** — same pattern for `io.Writer`.
- **`readWriteCounter`** — embeds `*readCounter` and `*writeCounter`, so it satisfies `ReadWriteCounter`; `NewReadWriteCounter` builds one from any `io.ReadWriter`.

The key detail for the consistency tests (`TestReadCountConsistency*` / `TestWriteCountConsistency*`): the byte total and operation count are updated together under one mutex, and `ReadCount`/`WriteCount` read them together, so a concurrent snapshot always satisfies `nops == n / numBytes`.
